# Section B results: reference checks, interval preservation, second heart-rate detector, subgroups

*Generated by `scripts/analysis/section_B.py`. Exploratory (MASTER_PLAN): no pass or fail. Intervals are 'by this method' (NeuroKit2 continuous wavelet: median over 12 leads on the original records, lead II only on digitised pages), never a clinical rate.*

**Limit of this check.** On the ORIGINAL signals (no damage, 500 Hz lead II) the alternative detectors disagree with the main heart-rate reference (difference > 5 bpm) on many recordings (`section_B_detector_check.py`):

| detector | differ_gt5bpm_of_100 | no_result |
|---|---|---|
| neurokit | 4 | 0 |
| pantompkins1985 | 31 | 0 |
| kalidas2017 | 19 | 0 |
| engzeemod2012 | 22 | 9 |
| elgendi2010 | 54 | 0 |
| hamilton2002 | 59 | 0 |
| christov2004 | 69 | 1 |
| rodrigues2021 | 83 | 0 |

So Pan-Tompkins is a noisy second opinion: its 'wrong' rate is already 13% on clean pages (main detector 3%), and no other detector tested is closer. Read the table as ranking and excess over the clean page, not as absolute rates: resolution level 5 and blur level 5 stay the worst; rotation level 5 also looks bad under this detector (and 21 pages give no output); JPEG, brightness and grid fading stay near the clean level. The main-detector verdict C1 was fixed in advance and is not changed by this check.
